clue.text: Archdeacon therefore participates in English service

indicators.note: the archdeacon and 'therefore' take part inside the abbreviation for English, so they sit within it

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title given to an archdeacon
so is a synonym of therefore

explanation.surface: A senior cleric joins in with a Church of England service.
explanation.walkthrough: VEN, short for Venerable, is the formal title of an archdeacon in the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, a church service held at dusk.

clue.text: Curse many a renegade

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, which crosswords treat as 'many'
a rat is someone who deserts or betrays their side

explanation.surface: Someone swears at a whole crowd of turncoats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' as D (500 in Roman numerals) is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild oath of annoyance, used as an exclamation like 'blast'.

clue.text: Vessel portrayed by painter in restaurant

indicators.note: the painter is placed inside the word for a restaurant

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant
RA stands for Royal Academician, a recognised painter

explanation.surface: A jug or ship is depicted by an artist dining out.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass container for serving wine or water, a kind of drinking vessel.

clue.text: Top clan involved in deal

indicators.note: the jumbled clan is put inside the word for deal

parts.note: deal is softwood timber such as pine

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of clan are mixed

explanation.surface: A leading clan is caught up in some business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved' scrambles the clan to NACL. 'Deal' looks like a business transaction but is the softwood timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is the highest point or peak, the summit of something.

clue.text: Why Di's aunt prepared a feast

indicators.note: prepared suggests the letters are made ready in a new arrangement

parts.note: the letters D, I and S as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone asks why Diana's aunt has laid on a banquet.
explanation.definitionFit: Whit Sunday, or Pentecost, is a Christian festival, a feast day in the church calendar.

clue.text: Villains taken in hand by shepherds

definitions.meaning: the hooked staffs that shepherds carry

explanation.definitionFit: Crooks are dishonest people, and a crook is also the hooked staff a shepherd holds.

clue.text: Bookkeepers in public are gloomy

indicators.note: the bookkeepers are placed inside the word for public

parts.note: overt means open or public
CAs are chartered accountants, the plural giving CAS

explanation.surface: Accountants working in the open are feeling down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Public' looks like a noun but is an adjective here, meaning open.
explanation.definitionFit: Overcast describes a dull, cloudy sky, so skies that are overcast look dark and dismal.

clue.text: A lass the match for two males?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a boy is a young male

explanation.surface: A girl is the equal of a pair of men.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomboy is a girl who enjoys rough, boisterous play.

clue.text: Where are you to stay permanently?

definitions.meaning: the reply to that question, said as two words: inside this place
to be an intrinsic, lasting part of something

explanation.definitionFit: To inhere is to exist inherently within something, and split in two it answers the question of location.

clue.text: To produce woollens is utterly silly

indicators.note: utterly suggests spoken or uttered, so the word for silly is heard

parts.note: a nit is a silly person, a nitwit

explanation.surface: Making jumpers is called completely foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterly' looks like 'completely' but means 'as uttered', the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to make garments by looping wool with needles.

clue.text: Warning of dire domination

indicators.note: dire means dreadful, so the letters are put in disarray

explanation.definitionFit: An admonition is a reprimand or caution, a gentle warning.

clue.text: Airman enters only to offer comfort

indicators.note: the airman goes into the word for only

parts.note: sole means only or single
AC is aircraftman, the lowest RAF rank

explanation.surface: A pilot joins only to console someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airman' suggests a pilot, but AC is the lowest RAF rank, aircraftman.
explanation.definitionFit: Solace is consolation, the comfort given to someone in distress.

clue.text: Everyone present admits silver is in fashion

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the silver goes inside the word for present

parts.note: there means present, in attendance
AG is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: All those attending confess silver is stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like 'gift' but means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very popular or trendy at present.

clue.text: Naturally, it relates to the racetrack

definitions.meaning: belonging to the racecourse, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means certainly, and literally means pertaining to a racing circuit.

clue.text: Society girl has metal aplenty

parts.note: gal is a colloquial word for a girl
ore is rock from which metal is got

explanation.surface: A debutante owns heaps of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore means in abundance, plentifully.

clue.text: Use the colander again, but keep the lid on

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to strain food is to drain it through a colander

explanation.surface: Sieve the vegetables a second time but keep them covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Again' becomes the prefix placed in front, though it follows in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to hold back or control, like keeping a lid on something.

clue.text: George Desmond finds crystal-lined cavities

parts.note: Des is a shortening of Desmond

explanation.surface: A man named George Desmond discovers some hollow rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Geodes are hollow rocks whose inner walls are lined with crystals.

clue.text: Flannel one can wash with

explanation.definitionFit: Soft soap is both flattery and a gentle liquid soap.

clue.text: The occasional worker is offhand

explanation.definitionFit: A casual is a temporary employee, and casual also means nonchalant.

clue.text: Reckon the man's taking notes in chapel

parts.note: to bet is to reckon or suppose
he's is a contraction of 'he is'
D and A are musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a man is carrying notes into chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: Bethesda is a common name for a Nonconformist chapel in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethesda is a name often given to a Methodist or Baptist meeting house.

clue.text: After knocking back drink Edward gets euphoric

indicators.note: knocking back means turning the word for drink backwards

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Edward feels joyful after downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means overjoyed, in high spirits.

clue.text: Stop putting workers on short time

explanation.definitionFit: To lay off is to quit, and a lay-off is a discharge of staff from work.

clue.text: Steps-up for a trainee teller

parts.note: a set of rungs, and the career route a junior bank clerk climbs

explanation.definitionFit: A ladder is a set of steps, and also a career route of promotion.

clue.text: Just the pitch for travelling show

parts.note: fair means just or equitable
a ground is a sports pitch

explanation.surface: Exactly the right site for a touring entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is the site where a travelling fair sets up, standing for the fair itself.

clue.text: Broke a piece of sculpture

explanation.definitionFit: Bust means penniless, and a bust is a sculpted head.

clue.text: Regina retired and had children

annotationWithheld.why: Regina retired and had children (4): R inside BED, but 'retired' must give BED and also signal the insertion, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Worsted cloth I made for a Muscovite male

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing worsted fabric

explanation.surface: Wool fabric and I are tailored for a Moscow man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei is a common Russian forename for a man.

clue.text: Faithful follower made me genial

indicators.note: made suggests the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter made me friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: A liegeman is a vassal sworn to serve a feudal lord, a loyal follower.
